doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Keeping extended vamps fresh and perfect-pitch singers
summary: Approach each song as new, draw sparks from the bass and drummer, and play with his brother Donald and Tabitha Pearson who have perfect pitch.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: A lot of the music that you recorded over the years has been — used extended vamps.
And were you ever in a position where you’re saying well we’ve been playing this vamp for eight minutes now, and I don’t know what to do with it anymore?

No. That’s the whole thing is I remember you have to — the thing is if you can get so you’re trying, every night, you’ve got to play certain songs anyway so you’ve got to try to approach the song, if you can, as if you’re playing it for the first time. If you can do that then that’s the key. You’re approaching the song for the first time and so it’s brand new, then you might try to find some different voicings and — but if you’ve got a very creative bass player and drummer and sometimes you use a guitarist, because I don’t like guitars that play chords, I want them to play those single notes, I don’t know what they call them, but so — and you might get a spark from the drummer or the bassist. And I’ve always been fortunate because my younger brother Donald, when he was singing in a group, he had perfect pitch and so we could just play. So he has perfect pitch, it doesn’t matter what chord I play. I can just play like I’m playing with a horn player. And then I found another young singer I heard, the drummer with Lee Pearson, he’s very talented. But his sister, Tabitha Pearson, I use her lately and she has perfect pitch. So you can be playing, what was that song, we do a song and it ends on a
You know with that flatted fifth but that won’t bother her, she was just singing. So, but you can’t do that with a lot of singers.
